question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7% per annum, respectively. Mahesh borrowed an amount of ₹4,60,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Mahesh after 2 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in rates = 7% − 3.5% = 3.5%

Difference in SI = P × R × T / 100

= 460000 × 3.5 × 2 / 100

= 460000 × 7 / 100 = 32200

**∴ Answer = ₹32200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal = 460000, Rates = 3.5% and 7%, Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI at 7% = (460000 × 7 × 2) ÷ 100 = 64400

⇒ SI at 3.5% = (460000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100 = 32200

⇒ Difference = 64400 − 32200 = 32200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹32200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Rate Difference Trick

Difference in SI can be directly calculated using difference of rates.

Linear Growth

Simple interest grows linearly with time.

Same Principal Case

If principal and time are same, compare only rates.
